title: 10 AI Predictions For 2026
gist: SemiWiki forum repost (by Daniel Nenni) of only the headlines and opening lines of a Forbes list of 10 AI predictions for 2026 (Forbes URL dated 2025-12-22): Anthropic IPOs while OpenAI does not, Sam Altman steps aside, China's AI chips erode Nvidia's dominance, depreciation schedules for AI chips become critical as debt funds the buildout, custom silicon proliferates, AGI hype cools, AI dominates the US midterms, pharma buys a protein-AI startup, and BCIs go mainstream as Neuralink's lead weakens. The text is a thin excerpt, so the supporting reasoning is largely missing, and it was reposted about nine months after the original, late in the year being forecast.

insights.claim: Anthropic is predicted to go public in 2026 while OpenAI will not IPO that year.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: An Anthropic IPO would be the first public-market pricing of a frontier AI lab. Watch for S-1 signals and how it re-rates private AI valuations and adjacent AI infrastructure names.
insights.quote: Anthropic will go public. OpenAI will not.

insights.claim: OpenAI and Anthropic are described as the fastest-growing and most capital-hungry venture-backed businesses in history, which is the stated reason public-market funding is on the table.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: The labs' capital needs exceed what private rounds can supply. Expect continued mega-raises, debt, or IPOs, all of which feed compute demand for chip suppliers.
insights.quote: they are the fastest-growing and most capital-hungry venture-backed businesses in history
insights.locator: AI research labs OpenAI and Anthropic

insights.claim: Sam Altman is predicted to step aside as CEO of OpenAI in 2026, a call the author admits is deliberately provocative given OpenAI's hypergrowth.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: A leadership change at OpenAI would shift the deal and partnership dynamics for its compute suppliers and investors. Treat this as a low-probability event with high impact.
insights.quote: Sam Altman will step aside as CEO of OpenAI.

insights.claim: Details of Ilya Sutskever's Safe Superintelligence (SSI) research are predicted to leak in 2026, prompting the big AI labs to meaningfully adjust their research roadmaps.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: A leaked research paradigm shift, for example away from pure scaling, could change the mix of compute demand and the relative positioning of the labs.
insights.quote: No technology company in the world is more shrouded in mystery than Ilya Sutskever’s Safe Superintelligence.

insights.claim: China's domestic AI chip sector is predicted to make significant strides in 2026, planting the seeds for the eventual decline of Nvidia's global dominance.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: This is a long-horizon risk to Nvidia's China revenue and pricing power. Watch Chinese accelerator capacity and adoption by Chinese hyperscalers.
insights.quote: planting the seeds for the eventual decline of Nvidia’s global dominance

insights.claim: US export controls on AI chips to China, called one of the most important decisions of the Biden administration, may have opposite long-term effects: short-term containment, but a long-term push toward Chinese self-sufficiency.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Export controls can backfire and act as industrial policy for Chinese chipmakers. Consider this when judging how durable US vendors' China exposure is.
insights.quote: Foreign policy decisions sometimes have dramatically different consequences in the short term versus the long term.

insights.claim: Many more AI companies are predicted to start building custom chips in 2026, breaking up today's concentration in which almost all AI runs on silicon from Nvidia, Google, AMD, Amazon and a few others.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: More in-house ASIC programs benefit custom-silicon design partners, EDA vendors and foundries, and put pressure on merchant GPU share over time.

insights.claim: Depreciation schedules for AI chips are predicted to become critically important in 2026, especially as debt plays a growing role in funding the AI infrastructure buildout.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: If GPUs are depreciated over a longer life than their real economic life, hyperscaler and neocloud earnings are overstated, and debt backed by GPUs as collateral carries hidden risk. Check the useful-life assumptions in 10-Ks.
insights.quote: Get ready to start hearing a lot about depreciation schedules for AI chips.

insights.claim: The growing use of debt rather than equity to fund AI data-center buildouts raises the importance of how long AI chips hold their value, which links accounting assumptions to credit risk.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Watch credit spreads and covenants on GPU-backed and data-center debt, where a shorter chip life would compress collateral values.
insights.quote: especially as debt plays a growing role in the AI infrastructure buildout

insights.claim: Talk of AGI and superintelligence is predicted to become less fashionable and less common in 2026, after 2025 began with sky-high expectations about AGI timelines.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Cooling AGI narratives could compress sentiment-driven multiples in AI equities even as spending continues. Monitor how labs and executives change their messaging.
insights.quote: Coming into 2025, expectations about AI’s trajectory and the timeline to artificial general intelligence were sky-high. The discourse was breathless.

insights.claim: AI is predicted to be one of the central issues of the 2026 US midterm elections, with complex politics around AI-driven job losses.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Job-loss politics raise regulatory and legislative risk for AI deployers and data-center buildouts. Track candidate platforms and state-level AI bills.
insights.quote: these midterm elections will be dominated by the topic of artificial intelligence

insights.claim: A large global pharma company is predicted to acquire one of the leading protein-AI startups in 2026, because AI-powered drug discovery started to genuinely work in 2025 after more than a decade of hype.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: M&A premiums for AI drug-discovery platforms are likely. Watch big-pharma BD activity and the valuations of protein-design startups.
insights.quote: something remarkable happened in 2025: the technology really started working

insights.claim: Brain-computer interfaces are predicted to move from a fringe field to a mainstream technology and startup category in 2026, while Neuralink's position as clear category leader becomes shakier.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Expect a rise in BCI venture funding and competitors to Neuralink. This is an emerging category to track for neurotech and medical-device exposure.
insights.quote: Neuralink’s position as the clear category leader will become shakier.
